title: On the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of the maximal multiple $ mathbb{Z} p$-extensions

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 1.1, definition of X(k_cyc) and X(\tilde k)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says: "We will denote by X(k_cyc) and X(\tilde k) the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian p-extension of k_cyc and k, respectively." This contradicts the earlier definition in the abstract/introduction, where X(\tilde k) is the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian p-extension over \tilde k. It should say "... of k_cyc and \tilde k, respectively."

The lemma states (σ|_k)^3(D_1)=D_1, (σ|_k)^4(D_1)=D_2, (σ|_k)^5(D_1)=D_3. Since σ^3 is the complex conjugation and the primes are defined by σ^3(𝔓_1)=overline{𝔓}_1, σ^4(𝔓_1)=overline{𝔓}_2, σ^5(𝔓_1)=overline{𝔓}_3, these images should be overline{D}_1, overline{D}_2, overline{D}_3, respectively. The same missing overlines occur in the proof.

The lemma concludes "K(G)=0 if and only if ... (a+b+c)^3+(a+b-c)^3 ≡ 0 mod p." This is the wrong condition: a cokernel of a square presentation matrix vanishes iff the determinant is nonzero modulo p, not zero. Indeed, later in Lemma 4.2.2 the paper uses |K| not≡ 0. The congruence should be not≡ 0.

With the fixed basis {[γ,x],[γ,y],[γ,z],[x,y],[y,z],[z,x]}, the image of H_2(D_2) represented by [γ x^a z^c, y] has coefficient vector (0,1,0,a,-c,0). The displayed matrix row is [0,1,a,-c,0,0], which shifts the entries a and -c into the wrong columns. This makes the subsequent row-reduction to the displayed block matrix inconsistent.

The text states: "Substituting c≡b-a in |K|, we obtain |K| ≡ 8(a+b)(a - ab + b^2)." But (a+b)^3+(a-b)^3 is 8(a^3+b^3)=8(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2). The square on a is missing; later the same expression "a - ab + b^2" is used again where a^2-ab+b^2 is required.

The proof says "Suppose that c not≡ 0... Since a-b+c not≡ 0 and a+b not≡ 0, we obtain |K| not≡ 0 in the case c≡0." The last clause "in the case c≡0" contradicts the hypothesis "Suppose that c not≡0"; it should say "in the case c not≡0."

The paper asserts the subgroup equality ⟨γ x^{a-c}, xy^{-1}z, xy⟩ = ⟨J(γ)γ, xy^{-1}z, xy⟩. In the abelian pro-p group Gal(\tilde k/k) with basis γ,x,y,z, J(γ)γ=γ^2 x^{a-b-c} y^{a+b-c} z^{a+b+c}. Matching elements of ⟨γ x^{a-c},xy^{-1}z,xy⟩ to this requires the extra factor 4(a+b) to vanish in Z_p. But the section only assumes a+b≡0 mod p and m=ord_p(a+b)>0, so a+b is not zero in Z_p. Thus the asserted equality is false and the claimed J-action as -1 on k_∞ is not established.

The lemma claims for i=1,2,3 that ⟨γ,xy,xz^{-1},I_i⟩=⟨γ,x^{a-b+c},xy,xz^{-1}⟩. For i=1, I_1=⟨γ⟩, so the left-hand side is just ⟨γ,xy,xz^{-1}⟩, which generally does not contain x^{a-b+c}. The displayed formula is only plausible for the conjugate inertias overline{I}_i, not I_i, indicating missing bars or a wrong statement.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 3.1.9, proof of triviality of X(k^(1))
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof says L_0/k is "unramified outside {q, overline{p}, q}". Since k^(1) is fixed by I_p and I_q, it is ramified only at overline{p} and overline{q}; hence the set should be {overline{p}, overline{q}}, not {q,overline{p},q}. The duplicated q and missing overline{q} make the stated ramification set incorrect.
